KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_AN: Sustained damage could reveal exactly what makes a shield give out—and how to make that happen faster. For science, naturally.
Even the toughest machines have their weak spots. Consistent strikes against vulnerable components could reveal a way to develop rounds that hit them where it hurts most. Metaphorically speaking.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_BU: Shredders manage rapid volleys with little downtime. Careful dismantling with a Raider Tool might preserve the firing assembly long enough to figure out how.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_CA: § Repurposes the Canto as a carbine, greatly improving stability and accuracy at the cost of agility.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_CH: Some ARC machines appear capable of absorbing energy before putting it back to use. The same principle might be worth testing on something a little less insulated.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_DR: A standard magazine does its job, but it can only hold so much. Getting familiar with a drum-fed design could reveal how that extra room is put to use, and where the same idea might fit elsewhere.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_FU: § Makes the weapon fully automatic, at the cost of accuracy and stability.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_HI: § Increases the velocity of the projectile fired.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_IN: Most explosives end with the detonation. Blaze Grenades have the good sense to keep causing trouble afterward. There may be something worth borrowing in that.
Impact damage is useful. Setting the problem on fire afterward feels like a reasonable improvement.
A burst has a beginning, a middle, and an end. The middle could probably use more bullets. Let's investigate.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_MA: § Removes the need to reload one projectile at a time.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_MO: § Increases the number of bullets loaded at a time, reducing reload time.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_PR: § Replaces the Anvil's bullets with rounds that split into four weaker projectiles.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_RA: The Equalizer is at its best when the beam stays exactly where the target would rather not have it. Maybe we can work with that.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_SC: Elevated firing positions provide clear sightlines. Osprey field data under those conditions could support development of improved magnification.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_SE: Fast-moving threats leave little margin for hesitation. Close encounters with Skulkers could reveal ways to improve paced combat effectiveness.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_SL: Shotgun engagements against drones offer a useful test of stopping power. Concentrating the full charge into a single projectile could produce far more decisive results.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_SP: Fast movement is useful right up until a weapon needs to come into play. A weapon that keeps up with the pace would be useful.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_ST: The Hairpin wastes very little motion between shots. That sort of efficiency gets more interesting once a scope is involved.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_TR: § Replaces the bullets with tracker rounds that briefly reveal the position of targets they hit.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_XR: Armor does a good job against bullets. Small explosions are less respectful of the arrangement. Combining the two might be worth exploring.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_BU: Burst weapons reward a good sense of timing. A few rounds with an Arpeggio against Pops and Fireballs should help build a feel for controlled volleys, and also provide some very satisfying target practice.
KeysToEntries.ST_ITEMDESC_RESEARCH_ASCENDEDUPGRADES_CH: Energy rounds behave differently from conventional rounds. Repeated use against ARC could reveal how stored energy might be concentrated into a more deliberate burst.
